How to calibrate a torque wrench in the field

Field calibration keeps a torque wrench accurate between laboratory checks. You will need a calibrated reference, a stable bench, and five uninterrupted minutes. Begin by setting the wrench to fifty percent of its range and taking three reference readings.

Record each reading and compare it against the reference tool. If the average deviation exceeds four percent, adjust the calibration screw a quarter turn and repeat. Most wrenches converge within two iterations. Log the final values with the date.

After calibration, dial the wrench down to its lowest setting to relax the spring, and store it in its case away from humidity. Repeat this procedure every twelve months or immediately after any drop, because impacts shift the internal mechanism.
